chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, who reported from Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Abdul Rahman al-Hijazi, who reported from his father, who reported from Isa ibn Abul Ward, from Ahmad ibn Abdul Aziz, who reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: "No deed is little when accompanied by taqwa, and how can that which is accepted (by God) be little?"

key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa -- God-consciousness, piety, and guarding oneself against sin
key_terms.يتقبل: Divine acceptance -- the concept that God accepts deeds performed with sincere intention and taqwa

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the value of good deeds performed with taqwa?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), as narrated through Imam al-Sadiq, teaches that no act of worship or good deed should be considered insignificant when it is performed with taqwa. He reinforces this with a rhetorical question: since God accepts deeds done with taqwa, they cannot be considered small. This teaching was directed at believers who might feel discouraged about the perceived smallness of their good deeds.
